summary: ApoIcarus provides reusable achievement state, persistence, deduplication, and rendering patterns. ApoMario provides lifecycle hooks, level timing, player points, enemy death, and menu navigation, but the target achievement state and route are not yet present.
limitations: The target ApoMario achievement class, its public members, store path/format, and final menu-panel routing are not present in the inspected source, so those implementation edges remain prospective.
The inspected code does not establish whether simulations, editor sessions, AI sessions, and replays are intended to count; the controls conservatively exclude them from achievement credit.
No build or tests were run because the workspace is read-only.

nodes.label: Gameplay-derived points, enemy kills, and survival time
Achievement store boundary
nodes.untrusted_input: User-editable local achievement store bytes, including malformed or unknown records
nodes.source: The Path supplied to the proposed ApoMarioStateAchievements constructor
nodes.sink: Achievement-store decoder and the in-memory unlocked-achievement collection used by getUnlockedAchievements() and the achievements renderer

nodes.label: Level-file boundary
nodes.untrusted_input: Locally edited or shared-server level bytes containing dimensions, entity counts, timing, and enemy records
nodes.sink: ApoMarioLevel state later consumed by recordRunEnd(ApoMarioLevel), including players, enemies, and time

nodes.label: Gameplay and cheat-state boundary
nodes.untrusted_input: Mutable local gameplay, replay, editor, debug, or AI-controlled values that can be tampered with to manufacture points, kills, or elapsed time
nodes.source: ApoMarioPanel and ApoMarioLevel gameplay lifecycle and enemy/player mutation paths
nodes.sink: Achievement progress updates and final achievement evaluation

nodes.label: The donor achievement state keeps unlocked entries in an ArrayList, loads persisted values, saves them, avoids duplicate additions, and renders earned entries in a dedicated view.
nodes.verification: Compare the target class against these donor responsibilities and test duplicate unlocks, reload/save persistence, and rendering.
nodes.task_relevance: Reuse this state/persistence/view structure for ApoMario, replacing donor achievement labels and storage transport with the required IDs and Path store.

nodes.label: ApoMarioPanel initializes menu/game-related models, starts a game by restarting the level, and dispatches the active model's think method from its main loop.
nodes.verification: Exercise normal start, restart, menu navigation, and game-loop transitions while asserting beginRun and end-of-run evaluation occur exactly once per run.
nodes.task_relevance: These are the target integration points for constructing/loading achievements, beginning a run, feeding live progress, and exposing the view.

nodes.label: ApoMarioLevel resets enemy collections, player state, timer, and level-start time while making or restarting a level; think decrements time and ends analysis when the timer reaches zero.
nodes.verification: Run two consecutive games and confirm the second run starts with zero points/kills/survival progress while previously unlocked IDs remain.
nodes.task_relevance: Use these lifecycle facts to isolate per-run progress and derive survival duration without carrying counters across runs.

nodes.label: Enemy death awards the selected player's points and marks the enemy dead; player points are mutable through a setter and readable through getPoints().
nodes.verification: Kill enemies through real collision paths and compare the achievement counter with distinct enemy death events and the level's player score.
nodes.task_relevance: The kill hook and player score are the gameplay facts that must feed ENEMIES_GOAL and POINTS_GOAL.

nodes.label: The existing level decoder reads width, height, and enemy count and uses them to allocate or iterate structures without visible feature-specific bounds in the inspected method.
nodes.verification: Feed edited level streams with negative, oversized, truncated, and excessive entity-count values and assert bounded rejection/reporting.
nodes.task_relevance: If achievement evaluation consumes level data from edited or shared files, malformed dimensions or counts can cause excessive allocation, iteration, or inconsistent achievement facts.

nodes.label: A user who edits the achievement store could inject arbitrary IDs, duplicate records, malformed text, or values intended to create false unlocks or corrupt the displayed state.
nodes.failure_behavior: Reject and report any record that is not one of POINTS_GOAL, ENEMIES_GOAL, or TIME_GOAL; the ApoMario integration falls back to an empty unlocked set before continuing gameplay.
nodes.verification: Use a temporary store containing each valid ID, unknown IDs, blank records, oversized records, duplicates, and invalid encodings; assert rejection is reported and valid gameplay still unlocks IDs.
nodes.task_relevance: The new persisted achievement state is a local trust boundary and must preserve unlock integrity against local cheating and tampering.

nodes.label: If achievement updates trust arbitrary mutable player, replay, editor, or AI state, a local cheater could manufacture score, kill, or time thresholds without real gameplay.
nodes.failure_behavior: Begin and update achievement runs only for ordinary non-replay, non-editor gameplay; for replay/editor/simulation inputs, normalize the run values to zero before final evaluation and still complete the run-end operation.
nodes.verification: Complete equivalent thresholds in ordinary play, replay, editor, simulation, and debug configurations; only ordinary play should unlock.
nodes.task_relevance: The task requires unlocks from real gameplay and per-run progress, so client-controlled alternate modes must not become achievement sources.

nodes.label: The achievement store decoder must accept only the three exact IDs, with at most 3 records and at most 64 UTF-8 bytes per record, and must reject and report unknown, blank, duplicate-format, oversized, or malformed records without substituting or clamping them.
nodes.failure_behavior: The decoder rejects and reports the invalid store input; the ApoMario integration uses an empty unlocked set as its stated fallback and continues the game so future valid unlocks are not suppressed.
nodes.verification: Property-test all three valid IDs, unknown IDs, blank/oversized/malformed records, more than 3 records, truncation, and duplicate entries.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects the integrity and authenticity of persisted unlocks while retaining the small feature-sized store.

nodes.label: The progress API must treat points, enemy kills, and survival duration as non-negative integers, reject negative or overflowing updates, and evaluate thresholds at or above 20,000 points, 3 kills, and 60,000 ms; beginRun must reset only per-run progress while leaving persisted unlocks intact.
nodes.failure_behavior: Reject and report invalid progress updates; at run start reset invalid or missing progress to zero before invoking the achievement state, and never clear already unlocked IDs.
nodes.verification: Test exact threshold, one-below threshold, repeated updates, negative values, integer overflow, and two-run reset/persistence behavior.
nodes.task_relevance: Implements the exact milestone semantics and prevents invalid caller values from changing achievement state.

nodes.label: Gameplay integration must update achievements from real non-replay gameplay events: score from the actual player score, kills from distinct enemy death events, and survival from active gameplay deltas; it must finalize against the given level's actual values at run end and save newly unlocked IDs across sessions.
nodes.failure_behavior: If a level or gameplay value is missing or invalid at the integration point, normalize it to zero before calling the achievement operation; still perform run-end evaluation and persistence, with no fabricated unlock.
nodes.verification: Instrument real gameplay and assert unlock timing at each threshold, final level-based evaluation, no replay/editor unlocks, and reload persistence.
nodes.task_relevance: Ensures unlocks occur during the run, do not carry progress across runs, and survive application restarts.

nodes.label: The level decoder must bound each decoded dimension to 1..500, each enemy/entity count to 0..5000, and each encoded field to the feature's numeric domain before allocation or retention; invalid values must be rejected and reported.
nodes.failure_behavior: The decoder rejects and reports invalid dimensions, counts, or fields before allocation; the gameplay integration substitutes a minimal valid level/run value before calling achievement evaluation so the primary game operation continues.
nodes.verification: Use boundary values and one-past-boundary values for every dimension, count, and feature-relevant numeric field, including truncated streams.
nodes.task_relevance: Prevents edited or shared level content from exhausting resources or supplying impossible achievement facts while allowing ordinary levels.

nodes.label: At the achievement-store load operation, parse a bounded UTF-8 line/record, require one exact known ID, retain no more than the 3 supported IDs, and report rejection; at panel initialization, use an empty set when loading fails.
nodes.failure_behavior: Reject/report invalid records in the parser; the ApoMario panel supplies an empty state as fallback and continues gameplay.
nodes.task_relevance: Concrete enforcement for persisted unlock integrity and bounded allocation.

nodes.label: At run start, invoke beginRun after level restart for ordinary play; at each real score, death, and active-time event, feed only normalized non-negative values; at run end call recordRunEnd with the current level and then saveAcrossSessions.
nodes.failure_behavior: For missing, invalid, replay, editor, or simulation values, substitute zero at the integration point and still call the run-end operation and save operation.
nodes.verification: Threshold timing, restart isolation, mode isolation, and persistence tests.
nodes.task_relevance: Binds unlocks to real gameplay and keeps per-run values separate from persisted unlocks.

nodes.label: At level decoding, validate dimensions in 1..500, entity/enemy counts in 0..5000, each record field before constructing entities, and reject/report invalid input before allocation; at achievement integration, substitute a minimal valid run value when level data is unavailable.
nodes.failure_behavior: Reject/report invalid decoder input before allocation; continue the game with the integration's stated minimal default rather than skipping achievement evaluation.
nodes.verification: Decoder fuzzing with oversized, negative, truncated, and boundary-valid level records.
nodes.task_relevance: Bounds untrusted content without rejecting ordinary feature-sized levels and protects achievement evaluation from malformed level data.

nodes.label: Run a focused integration suite covering all three exact IDs, threshold boundaries, unlock timing, run reset, persistence reload, duplicate unlocks, corrupted stores, replay/editor exclusion, and malformed level inputs.
nodes.verification: Automated tests plus manual menu rendering and restart/session checks.
nodes.task_relevance: Verifies the proposed achievement dataflow and each trust-boundary control.

nodes.label: The inspected ApoMario target tree does not establish the achievement store path, file format, or atomic-save behavior; the implementation must choose and verify these integration details.
nodes.verification: Inspect the implemented constructor call and store read/write code, then test restart and corrupted-store recovery.
nodes.task_relevance: These choices determine how persisted unlock integrity and recovery are enforced.

nodes.label: The inspected ApoMario symbol graph does not establish a single ordinary-game run-end callback that always executes before menu return, death, timeout, win, restart, or new-level transitions.
nodes.verification: Trace and test every termination path, including timeout, player death, win, escape, restart, and new level.
nodes.task_relevance: Without this edge, final evaluation and saving could be missed on some run termination paths.
